'''Majda's model''' is a qualitative model (in [[mathematical physics]]) introduced by [[Andrew Majda]] in 1981 for the study of interactions in the combustion theory of shock waves and explosive chemical reactions.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Majda, Andrew|title=A qualitative model for dynamic combustion|journal=SIAM J. Appl. Math.|volume=41|issue=1|pages=70–93|doi=10.1137/0141006|year=1981}}</ref>

The following definitions are with respect to a [[Cartesian coordinate system]] with 2 variables. For [[function (mathematics)|function]]s <math>u(x,t)</math>, <math>z(x,t)</math> of one spatial variable <math>x</math> representing the [[Lagrangian and Eulerian specification of the flow field|Lagrangian specification of the fluid flow field]] and the [[time]] variable <math>t</math>, functions <math>f(w)</math>, <math>\phi (w)</math> of one variable <math>w</math>, and positive constants <math>k, q, B</math>, the '''Majda model''' is a pair of coupled [[partial differential equation]]s:<ref name=Humphreys>{{cite journal|author=Humphreys, Jeffrey|author2=Lyng, Gregory|author3=Zumbrun, Kevin|title=Stability of viscous detonations for Majda's model|journal=Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena|volume=259|year=2013|pages=63–80 |arxiv=1301.1260|doi=10.1016/j.physd.2013.06.001|bibcode=2013PhyD..259...63H|s2cid=119301730}}</ref>

:<math>\frac{\partial u(x,t)}{\partial t} + q \cdot \frac{\partial z(x,t)}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial f(u(x,t))}{\partial x} = B \cdot \frac{\partial^2u(x,t)}{\partial x^2}</math>
:<math>\frac{\partial z(x,t)}{\partial t} = - k \cdot \phi (u(x,t)) \cdot z(x,t)</math><ref name=Humphreys/>

:the unknown function <math>u = u(x,t)</math> is a [[Lumped element model|lumped variable]], a scalar variable formed from a complicated nonlinear average of various aspects of density, velocity, and temperature in the exploding gas;
:the unknown function <math>z = z(x,t) \in [0,1]</math> is the [[Mass fraction (chemistry)|mass fraction]] in a simple one-step chemical reaction scheme;
:the given flux function <math>f = f(w)</math> is a nonlinear convex function;
:the given ignition function <math>\phi = \phi (w)</math> is the starter for the chemical reaction scheme;
:<math>k</math> is the constant [[reaction rate]];
:<math>q</math> is the constant heat release;
:<math>B</math> is the constant [[diffusivity]].<ref name=Humphreys/>

{{blockquote|Since its introduction in the early 1980s, Majda's simplified "qualitative" model for detonation ... has played an important role in the mathematical literature as test-bed for both the development of mathematical theory and computational techniques. Roughly, the model is a <math>2 \times 2</math> system consisting of a [[Burgers' equation]] coupled to a [[chemical kinetics]] equation. For example, Majda (with [[Phillip Colella|Colella]] & Roytburd) used the model as a key diagnostic tool in the development of fractional-step computational schemes for the Navier-Stokes equations of compressible reacting fluids ...<ref>{{cite web|author=Lyng, Gregory D.|title=Spectral and nonlinear stability of viscous strong and weak detonation waves in Majda's qualitative model|year=2015|url=http://www.icders.org/ICDERS2015/abstracts/ICDERS2015-283.pdf}}</ref>}}
